name: Orléanist
summary: Orleanism is the French liberal, bourgeois, constitutional-monarchist current that backed the House of Orléans and came to power with the July Monarchy of 1830-1848. It held that a king should rule under a constitution and the law, not by divine right, with press freedom, legal opposition and curbs on Church influence, but also a limited franchise. It split into a conservative Resistance wing (Perier, Guizot) and a more liberal Movement wing (Laffitte).
scope: The Orléanism of the Orléans branch's constitutional monarchists, centred on its zenith in the July Monarchy (1830-48): Louis-Philippe, the Resistance party of Casimir Perier, Guizot and Thiers, and the more liberal Movement wing of Laffitte and Odilon Barrot, as Britannica and Aston (History Today) describe it. Britannica names the later fusion with the Legitimists around the Count of Paris after 1883 only as a continuation of support for the Orléans claimant; its positions are not recorded as a separate strand, and the Action Française variant is excluded.
